sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue, 22nd ed., entry 'Gamit' (via the Internet Archive).
sources.note: Alternate names Gamati, Gameti, Gamith, Gamta, Gamti, Gavit; dialects none known, 'reportedly similar to Mawchi'; NT 1982; no grammar or dictionary listed.

sources.citation: Chaudhari, Vikram G. 2009. Chaudhari, Dhodiya, Gamit ane Kunkana bhasha: ek abhyas [Chaudhari, Dhodiya, Gamit and Kunkana languages: a study; in Gujarati]. PhD thesis, Dept. of Gujarati, Veer Narmad South Gujarat University, Surat (guide Jagdish M. Gurjar). 314 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/324098.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 4 (thesis pp. 123-183) is the phonology: 4.7 Gamit vowels pp. 137-141 (8 vowels + 8 nasalised, following Fr. Raymond Chauhan's grammar), 4.7.1 vowel changes, 4.11 Gamit consonants pp. 162-167, 4.15 pronunciation differences p. 173, 4.16 p. 176; ch. 7 conclusions pp. 271-278. No statement on where word stress falls in Gamit. The only 'stress'-type remarks: p. 130-131 on Chaudhari ('the vowel is not pronounced clearly open, its svarabhar [stress] passes to the preceding vowel'; an extra 'bharank-vala' [weighted] vowel), and pp. 172-173, 177 and ch. 7 pp. 272-273: 'bharank-vala dhvanighatak'…

sources.citation: Borkar, I. S. (ed.), Bhagwandas Patel, Dilip Gamit & Sonal Baxi. 2008. Gamit Pictorial Glossary (English-Gamit). Mysore: Central Institute of Indian Languages & Vadodara: Bhasha Research and Publication Centre.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Picture vocabulary for schools; no phonological introduction; a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable/pronunciation: nothing.

sources.citation: Gamit, Sundarbhai Chhotubhai. 2025. Tribal folksongs of Gamit tribe: a critical study [in Gujarati]. PhD thesis, Dept. of Gujarati, M.S. University of Baroda (guide Pundlik C. Pawar). 377 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/711846.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.19 'Gamit boli/bhasha no vyakaranagat abhyas' pp. 85-95: eleven Gujarati > Gamit sound correspondences (gh jh dh dh bh > g j d d b; s/sh > h; initial h lost; l > n; cluster simplification; final 'h' with word-final vowels), then number, gender, case. Nothing on stress or accent. Annexure p. 342 lists 14 books on the Gamit incl. Fr. R. A. Chauhan's 1997 grammar.

sources.citation: Patel, Rita B. 2019. Folklore of Gamit tribe: a study of socio-cultural ethos as expressed in their songs and tales. PhD thesis, Dept. of English, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University (guide Keyur Parekh). Shodhganga hdl 10603/319210.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pp. 105-106 'Gamit language': Grierson's classification, limited vocabulary, aspirates bh gh dh dropped, one verb paradigm of 'to eat'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gamit, Umesh R. 2010. Gamit samaj na lokgito: ek abhyas [Folk songs of the Gamit community; in Gujarati]. PhD thesis, VNSGU Surat (guide Naresh Shukla). 448 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/327426; synopsis on Shodhgangotri (archive.org sgng.2275).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Folk-song thesis; only prelims and bibliography downloaded (legacy-font text layer, unreadable); synopsis has no phonology. Not a phonological description.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Gamti or Gamatadi' sketch p. 119, specimens nos. 38-39 pp. 119-122.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Gamti sketch (p. 119) gives only sound correspondences (aspirates not hardened, l not > n, intervocalic h dropped) and inflexion; the volume's front-matter convention 'when it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used' is never applied in the Gamti specimens (0 acute accents in the scanned of pp. 119-122).
